items.topic: Extraction scope — what moves to vrooli-emulator
items.context: The livedesktop package is well-isolated and ready to extract. However, there are two possible scopes: (1) extract only the session/display management (livedesktop), or (2) also unify smoketest's display management under the emulator. Smoketest currently uses xvfb-run independently. Unifying would eliminate duplication but increases extraction complexity.

options.label: Livedesktop only — extract session management, VNC proxy, actions, and platform backends
options.rationale: Cleanest extraction boundary, minimal risk. Smoketest can migrate later as a follow-up.

options.label: Livedesktop + smoketest display — unify all display management in the emulator
options.rationale: Eliminates duplication immediately, but smoketest has different needs (headless, no VNC) that may complicate the API.

items.context: vrooli-emulator needs to expose its session API to consumers (scenario-to-desktop, deployment-manager, future scenarios). The current livedesktop uses HTTP REST + WebSocket (for VNC). Options are: keep HTTP/WS as-is, add gRPC for programmatic consumers, or use both.

options.label: HTTP REST + WebSocket only (same as current livedesktop)
options.rationale: Zero protocol migration cost. WebSocket is already required for VNC. Simple for UI consumers and CLI.

options.label: gRPC for service-to-service, HTTP+WS for UI/CLI
options.rationale: Stronger typing and streaming for programmatic consumers, but adds a second protocol to maintain.

items.context: The livedesktop UI components (VncCanvas, LiveDesktopDrawer, DesktopControlsMenu, MetricsBar, etc.) and Zustand store currently live in scenario-to-desktop's UI. These need to be available to any scenario that wants to embed a desktop viewer. Options differ in how the UI is distributed.

options.label: vrooli-emulator owns a UI package; consumers import components
options.rationale: Single source of truth for desktop viewer UI. Consumers compose it into their own layouts. Standard library approach.

options.label: vrooli-emulator provides API only; each consumer rebuilds UI
options.rationale: Maximum flexibility but duplicates the noVNC integration work. Only makes sense if different consumers need radically different UIs.

options.label: vrooli-emulator ships its own standalone UI + embeddable components
options.rationale: Emulator gets a full management UI (session list, viewer, controls) AND exports key components for embedding. Most complete but highest initial effort.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own UI ownership model

items.notes: Using an iframe or similar technique probably best fits how we typically do this sort of thing. E.g. app-monitor, deployment-manager

items.context: Human validation (visual inspection of desktop apps) is needed by both scenario-to-desktop (smoketest review) and deployment-manager (approval workflows). The emulator could provide validation primitives (screenshot capture, side-by-side comparison, annotation) as part of its API, or leave validation logic to consumers.

options.label: Emulator provides capture primitives only; validation logic stays in consumers
options.rationale: Emulator stays focused on display/session management. deployment-manager and scenario-to-desktop own their validation UX.

options.label: Emulator includes a validation subsystem (capture + comparison + annotation + verdict)
options.rationale: Centralizes validation so every consumer gets the same capabilities, but scope-creeps the emulator beyond display management.

items.text: The PlatformBackend interface in platform.go is already designed for extraction — it documents local backends (linux-xvfb, future windows-qemu, android-emulator) and remote backends (remote-macos, remote-ios) with explicit design constraints for service extraction: URLs over byte blobs, stateless callers, backend-owned session state. This interface can move to vrooli-emulator nearly unchanged.

The dependency research (desktop-release-control-plane-audit) is completed and confirms the release pipeline is deployment-manager → scenario-to-desktop → LPBS. The emulator extraction does NOT affect this pipeline — livedesktop is not in the build/deploy path. This means extraction has low blast radius for the production desktop flow.

livedesktop's only internal dependency is the procmetrics package (process monitoring). This is a small, focused package that should either move to vrooli-emulator or become a shared library. All other scenario-to-desktop packages (pipeline, build, deploy, signing, etc.) have zero coupling to livedesktop.

The artifact launch model currently works by: (1) session start with optional app_path, (2) if empty, auto-discover from latest build artifact via findArtifact(scenarioName), (3) LaunchApp spawns process on virtual display. After extraction, vrooli-emulator would need callers to provide the app_path explicitly (no cross-scenario build artifact knowledge), or accept a scenario name and use service discovery to find the build output path.

The captures system (screenshots, recordings) in scenario-to-desktop has its own handler and store at api/captures/. It's partially coupled to livedesktop (screenshots come from sessions) but also stores pipeline-generated captures independently. This needs a clear ownership split during extraction.
